name: Airfoil Design Optimization via ML-Based Surrogate Models
description: Develop machine learning models to simulate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airfoil design, replacing computationally expensive numerical methods. The goal is to predict physical simulation outputs (e.g., velocity, pressure, lift, drag) based on input geometries and boundary conditions, while optimizing computational efficiency, accuracy, and physical consistency.

cr:input.name: AirfRANS dataset
cr:input.description: Unstructured mesh data representing 2D simulation domains. Includes positions (x, y coordinates of mesh nodes), inlet velocity (scalar, e.g., 10 m/s), distance to the airfoil (scalar), normals (vector values representing surface orientation), and boundary conditions (e.g., angle of attack, Reynolds number).

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: Predictions for velocity components (u_x, u_y), pressure divided by specific mass (p_s), turbulent kinematic viscosity (nu_t), and derived quantities (lift coefficient C_L, drag coefficient C_D).

field.name: u_x
field.description: Velocity component in the x direction. Example: 0.5.

field.name: u_y
field.description: Velocity component in the y direction. Example: -0.3.

field.name: p_s
field.description: Pressure divided by specific mass. Example: 101325.
